statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-21717 is a HashDoS in V8: integer-like strings hash to their numeric value, so an attacker can force collisions in V8's string table, for example through JSON.parse() on attacker-controlled input. Node.js fixed it for 22.x in 22.22.2, the 2026-03-24 security release (https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/march-2026-security-releases), with the V8 backports 30a3ab11e2, e3f4d6a42e, 7dc00fa5f4 and 076acd052d and commit 6f14ee5101, 'build,test: test array index hash collision' (https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/6f14ee5101), which enables the seeded array index hash in Node.js's default build configuration; each carries this CVE id. Release notes: https://nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v22.22.2. The CVE record (https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-21717) lists 22.x releases through 22.22.1 as affected. We read the node binary in every published DHI nodejs-22 package for Alpine 3.23 on x86_64 and aarch64: 22.22.2-r0 is the first that reports Node.js v22.22.2; 22.22.0-r0 and 22.22.1-r0 report Node.js 22.22.0 and 22.22.1. We also ran upstream's regression test for the fix (test/pummel/test-array-hash-collision.js) against every published Alpine 3.23 aarch64 build: it fails, reporting a hash flooding regression, on 22.22.0-r0 and 22.22.1-r0, and passes on 22.22.2-r0 through 22.23.5-r0. Both earlier builds predate the fix, so the range starts at 0.
